import sys, json, base64, time, urllib.request, urllib.error

# Wall clock starts before the first byte is read: the read lane bounds itself
# against the cell's OWN operation timeout (see DEADLINE below), and everything
# this process does counts against it.
STARTED = time.monotonic()

ENDPOINT = "${MEMORY_EMBED_ENDPOINT:-https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/embeddings}"
MODEL = "${MEMORY_EMBED_MODEL:-google/gemini-embedding-2}"
DIM = int("${MEMORY_EMBED_DIM:-1024}")
API_KEY = "${MEMORY_EMBED_API_KEY:-}" or "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}"
# App attribution: the llm cells send these as params, this code cell is the
# OTHER call path and used to send nothing — which is why only part of the
# traffic showed up attributed in the provider dashboard.
HTTP_REFERER = "${OPENROUTER_HTTP_REFERER:-https://meclaw.ai}"
X_TITLE = "${OPENROUTER_X_TITLE:-MeClaw}"
BIN_VERSION = "v1"

stdin_doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = stdin_doc["body"]
# This cell's own configuration arrives on the same stdin document (`params`,
# always present). The literal beside each name is the shipped default -- the
# same number the template config and `contract.settings` carry, pinned against
# each other by a test.
P = stdin_doc.get("params") or {}


def _int(key, default):
    """A knob left null or blank is 'not configured', not a crash."""
    v = P.get(key, default)
    if v is None:
        return default
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    try:
        return int(v)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default


# TWO timeouts, because the two lanes have opposite trade-offs (GH #146):
#
#   write lane (bulk corpus) -- throughput. A slow batch is not urgent and its
#   rows simply stay queued for the next backfill, so a tight bound that frees
#   the concurrency slot is the cheap answer.
#
#   read lane (the query vector recall waits on) -- latency-critical, but the
#   loss on failure is the whole semantic leg of a four-leg fan. Measured under
#   ten parallel colonies: three of thirty questions burned the 20 s bound while
#   a single call against the same provider took 0.26 s -- CPU contention on the
#   box, not a dead endpoint. So this lane gets a longer bound AND a retry: a
#   second attempt costs a fraction of what a missing leg costs in answer
#   quality, and "a timeout needs a retry" is the ruling behind this file.
TIMEOUT_S = _int("timeout_ms", 20000) / 1000.0
QUERY_TIMEOUT_S = _int("query_timeout_ms", 30000) / 1000.0
QUERY_RETRIES = max(0, _int("query_retries", 1))
QUERY_BACKOFF_S = max(0, _int("query_retry_backoff_ms", 250)) / 1000.0
# The retry may NEVER push the read lane past the cell's operation timeout: a
# killed process is silence, and silence hangs recall's fan-in forever, which is
# strictly worse than the degraded answer this retry exists to avoid. So the
# lane reads its own `external_timeout_ms` and keeps a reserve for spawn plus
# the final write. An operator who raises query_timeout_ms without raising the
# operation timeout loses attempts, never the answer.
EXTERNAL_TIMEOUT_S = _int("external_timeout_ms", 65000) / 1000.0
DEADLINE_RESERVE_S = 2.0
MIN_ATTEMPT_S = 1.0
DEADLINE = STARTED + max(MIN_ATTEMPT_S, EXTERNAL_TIMEOUT_S - DEADLINE_RESERVE_S)


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def park(reason=None):
    if reason:
        sys.stderr.write("embed: %s\n" % reason)
    emit([])


def first_text(doc):
    for m in doc.get("messages", []):
        if m.get("text"):
            return m.get("text")
    return ""


def binarize(vec):
    """float vector -> packed sign bits -> base64 (1024 dims = 128 bytes).
    Deterministic and dimension-agnostic; the store only ever compares blobs of
    the same model_id, so the packing never has to be self-describing. ONE
    function for both lanes: a query vector packed differently than the stored
    vectors would make hamming() measure noise."""
    bits = bytearray((len(vec) + 7) // 8)
    for i, v in enumerate(vec):
        if v > 0:
            bits[i // 8] |= 1 << (7 - (i % 8))
    return base64.b64encode(bytes(bits)).decode("ascii")


def hop_usage(head, usage):
    """Token accounting rides the SAME hop field the llm cells write
    (`tokens_prompt`), so the message log sums one way over both call paths.
    Embeddings bill the prompt side only; a response without a usage block
    leaves the field out rather than booking a zero."""
    tokens = usage.get("prompt_tokens") if isinstance(usage, dict) else None
    if isinstance(tokens, int) and not isinstance(tokens, bool):
        return dict(head, tokens_prompt=tokens)
    return head


def call_endpoint(texts, timeout_s):
    """Returns (vectors, usage, error). Never raises — the caller decides whether
    a failure is silence (write lane) or an explicit degraded answer (read lane).
    `usage` is whatever the response carried, also on the mismatch error path:
    that call was billed even though its vectors are unusable."""
    # Provider exclusion: OpenRouter routes this model across several
    # providers, and Nebius Token Factory answered embedding calls with
    # latencies far outside any sane operation timeout -- a routed batch
    # simply timed out and left its rows queued. Excluding the one provider
    # is cheaper than raising the timeout for every other one.
    body = {"model": MODEL, "input": texts, "dimensions": DIM,
            "provider": {"ignore": ["nebius"]}}
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        ENDPOINT, data=json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8"),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json",
                 "HTTP-Referer": HTTP_REFERER, "X-Title": X_TITLE})
    if API_KEY:
        req.add_header("Authorization", "Bearer " + API_KEY)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout_s) as resp:
            payload = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return None, None, "endpoint returned HTTP %s" % e.code
    except Exception as e:
        return None, None, "endpoint unreachable (%s)" % type(e).__name__
    usage = payload.get("usage")
    vectors = [r.get("embedding") for r in payload.get("data", []) if isinstance(r, dict)]
    vectors = [v for v in vectors if isinstance(v, list) and v]
    if len(vectors) != len(texts):
        return None, usage, "endpoint returned %d vectors for %d inputs" % (len(vectors), len(texts))
    return vectors, usage, None


def call_query(text):
    """The read lane's bounded retry loop. Returns (vectors, usage, error,
    attempts). A retry is NOT a replacement for fail-open: whatever comes out of
    here, the caller still answers — degraded if the last attempt failed."""
    attempts = 0
    vectors = usage = None
    err = "read lane made no attempt"
    for i in range(QUERY_RETRIES + 1):
        remaining = DEADLINE - time.monotonic()
        if remaining < MIN_ATTEMPT_S:
            # Out of budget before the attempt: answering degraded NOW is the
            # only thing left that is not silence.
            err = "%s; no budget left for attempt %d" % (err, i + 1)
            break
        vectors, usage, err = call_endpoint([text], min(QUERY_TIMEOUT_S, remaining))
        attempts += 1
        if not err:
            return vectors, usage, None, attempts
        # Every failed attempt is a line, not just the final verdict: a lane
        # that recovered on its second try is invisible otherwise, and that is
        # exactly the signal that says whether the retry is earning its keep.
        sys.stderr.write("embed: query attempt %d/%d failed — %s\n"
                         % (i + 1, QUERY_RETRIES + 1, err))
        if i < QUERY_RETRIES:
            time.sleep(max(0.0, min(QUERY_BACKOFF_S, DEADLINE - time.monotonic())))
    return None, usage, err, attempts


try:
    payload = json.loads(first_text(d))
except Exception:
    park()
if not isinstance(payload, dict):
    park()

# ------------------------------------------------------------- query mode
# The read lane ALWAYS gets an answer. Silence would hang recall's fan-in
# forever, so a dead embedder is reported as degraded=true and recall fuses
# the remaining three legs. (The write lane below keeps the opposite rule.)
if isinstance(payload.get("query"), dict):
    q = payload["query"]
    text = str(q.get("text") or "")
    head = {"route": "equery", "phase": "query"}

    def answer(vector, degraded, error=None, usage=None):
        if error:
            sys.stderr.write("embed: query degraded — %s\n" % error)
        body = {"vector": vector, "degraded": degraded, "model_id": MODEL,
                "dim": DIM, "recall_id": str(q.get("recall_id") or "")}
        if error:
            body["error"] = error
        emit([{"header": hop_usage(head, usage),
               "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "e-query",
                             "text": json.dumps(body)}]}])

    if not text:
        answer(None, True, "empty query text")
    vectors, usage, err, tries = call_query(text)
    if err:
        answer(None, True, "%s (after %d attempt(s))" % (err, tries), usage)
    answer(binarize(vectors[0]), False, None, usage)

# ------------------------------------------------------------- write mode
items = [i for i in payload.get("items", [])
         if isinstance(i, dict) and i.get("embedding_id") and i.get("text")]
if not items:
    park()

# Degradation rule: the hive must NEVER hard-fail on a dead embedder. Any
# failure here is a logged no-op — the embedding rows stay status='queued' and
# the nightly backfill retries them. That backfill IS this lane's retry, which
# is why the in-process one belongs to the read lane only: repeating a batch
# here would pay twice for rows a later run picks up for free.
vectors, usage, err = call_endpoint([i["text"] for i in items], TIMEOUT_S)
if err:
    park("%s — %d rows stay queued" % (err, len(items)))

out = []
for item, vec in zip(items, vectors):
    args = {"operation": "update", "table": "embeddings",
            "set": {"blob": binarize(vec), "model_id": MODEL, "dim": len(vec),
                    "binarization_version": BIN_VERSION, "status": "ready"},
            "where": {"id": item["embedding_id"]}}
    # ONE batched call, ONE bill: the usage rides on the first update only.
    # Repeating it per row would book the batch cost N times.
    head = {"route": "estore", "phase": "embedded"}
    out.append({"header": head if out else hop_usage(head, usage),
                "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "e-upd",
                              "text": json.dumps(args)}]})
emit(out)

model.description: Embedding model id; must match the active row in emb_models (MEMORY_EMBED_MODEL)

dim.description: Requested embedding dimensions; must match emb_models.dim (MEMORY_EMBED_DIM)

timeout_ms.description: WRITE lane (params.timeout_ms): A-timeout of one bulk corpus embedding call. Throughput, not latency -- a failed batch leaves its rows status='queued' and the nightly backfill picks them up, so a tight bound that frees the concurrency slot is the cheap answer.

query_timeout_ms.description: READ lane (params.query_timeout_ms): A-timeout of ONE query-embedding attempt. Deliberately more generous than the write lane (GH #146): the query vector is what recall's semantic leg waits on, and losing it costs a whole leg of the four-leg fan.

query_retries.description: READ lane (params.query_retries): extra attempts after the first before the lane answers degraded. 0 switches the retry off; the fail-open contract is unaffected either way -- a retry is not a replacement for it. The write lane has no counterpart on purpose: its retry is the nightly backfill.

query_retry_backoff_ms.description: READ lane (params.query_retry_backoff_ms): pause between two read-lane attempts. Short by design -- the measured failure is CPU contention on the box, not a rate limit.

description.purpose: The semantic leg's generation side, both directions: it embeds texts through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and binarises the returned float vectors into packed sign bits. Write lane persists them; read lane hands the query vector back to recall. ONE binarisation function serves both — a query packed differently than the corpus would make hamming() measure noise.
description.use_when: Behind extract-glue (fresh facts) and dream-glue (nightly backfill) on the write side, and behind recall on the read side (tier-1 query vector).
description.not_in_scope: No similarity search (that is the store's similar op), no model management beyond the configured id, and no retry on the WRITE lane -- a failed batch leaves its rows queued for the next backfill, which is that lane's retry. The bounded in-process retry belongs to the read lane alone.
description.emits_meaning: route estore (write lane): one update per embedded row. NOTHING when the endpoint is down — that is the degradation rule, the rows simply stay queued. route equery (read lane): the query vector, and on failure the SAME message with vector=null and degraded=true -- after query_retries+1 bounded attempts, each failed one on stderr and the final verdict as a degraded line, so a lane that gave up is greppable in the colony log instead of visible only in the flag. The read lane never stays silent: recall's fan-in waits for a fixed set of legs and silence would hang it forever. Both routes carry hop.tokens_prompt whenever the response reported usage — the same accounting field the llm cells write, so the message log sums one way over both call paths. A batched write lane bills ONCE, on the first update, never once per row.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: a tool_call whose args are either {items:[{embedding_id, text}]} (write) or {query:{text, recall_id}} (read). Store replies and anything unparseable are swallowed.
examples: {items:[{embedding_id:'e1',text:'diet keto'}]} -> update embeddings set blob=<base64 128B>, dim=1024, status='ready' where id='e1'
{query:{text:'what does the user eat'}} -> route equery {vector:'<base64>', degraded:false, model_id, dim}
endpoint down, write lane -> empty multi-send + had_stderr, rows keep status='queued'
endpoint down, read lane -> route equery {vector:null, degraded:true, error:'endpoint unreachable (URLError)'}
first attempt times out, second succeeds -> route equery {vector:'<base64>', degraded:false} plus ONE stderr line about the failed attempt
